name: AMPLIFY ENERGY

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That the refusal costs a genuine finding. The royalty rate on Beta has been CUT IN HALF, effective 2026-11-01, by a dated regulatory action that appears in no historical financial statement and that no backward-looking model can see; Bairoil operating cost is down more than $20 million annualised; production is up 15% from Q1; and the company is buying its own stock at $4.35 saying it is below intrinsic value. Those are four independent, verifiable improvements against a $167 million market capitalisation and no debt.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 operating cash flow with a full quarter of SCRR and the Bairoil savings in them - the first period in which the improved economics are actually reported rather than forecast.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The improvements are visible and verified; what is not visible is the cash. Operating cash flow in Q3 was $3.1 million and total liquidity is $25.0 million, so the gap between improved unit economics and consolidated cash generation has not yet closed.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The cost of equity, which is the whole valuation on a levered single-basin producer, and which the schema cannot reach. I also could not obtain a current PV-10 or PDP decline rate from the quarterly filing; those come with the 10-K, and per the CRGY rule an E&P should be anchored on PV-10 and decline before any DCF gap is read at all.

what_changed: Q3 results, 2026-11-09, and the stock rose 26.4% in five days. The genuinely new and dated item is ENHANCED BETA ROYALTY RELIEF: building on the End of Life relief secured in May 2026, Amplify obtained Special Case Royalty Relief at Beta effective 2026-11-01, taking the royalty rate on ALL Beta production to approximately 12.4%, down from 24.8% before any relief. The suspension threshold also rose to about $92 per BOE on a trailing twelve-month average from about $80. Unlike the prior framework, SCRR does not erode as volumes rise, so it improves drilling economics and extends field life. Also: no outstanding revolver debt at 2026-09-30, but liquidity of only $25.0 million ($10.0 million cash plus about $15.0 million of availability); a net LOSS of $18.9 million on derivative movements against net income of $17.3 million in Q2; operating cash flow of just $3.1 million in the quarter; and a material weakness still being remediated, named in the company's own risk language.
consensus_case: Amplify has simplified to two producing assets - the Beta field offshore southern California and the Bairoil CO2 flood in Wyoming - after divesting its non-core positions, and both are improving. Third-quarter production averaged 7.4 MBopd, 100% oil, up 9% sequentially and 15% from Q1, on new wells (C29 and C16, each about 370 gross Bopd with ten-month payouts and IRRs above 150%) plus royalty relief. Bairoil lease operating expense fell $3.0 million sequentially and $5.2 million year over year, with annualised savings now forecast above $20 million against 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $10.8 million, up $2.2 million sequentially, despite $9.7 million of realised derivative losses, and the company says hedge prices are higher in 2027. It carries NO drawn debt and has bought back about 4.0% of its shares at a $4.35 average. At a $167 million market capitalisation against an improving two-asset base, holders are buying an operational turnaround.
base_case_rationale: The discount rate is not a measurement and the cash-flow history is not this company, so no number is admissible. Beta is 0.256 with an R-squared of 0.031, sourced `yahoo_rescaled`, producing a 6.449% WACC for a sub-$200 million offshore California oil producer with $25 million of total liquidity, a single federal-waters asset, a pipeline-incident history and an unremediated material weakness. Per the standing ISBA and FLNG rule, a beta below roughly 0.2-0.3 on a name like this is a failed measurement rather than a low-risk business, and because the schema has no cost-of-equity field the verdict is the only available output. Separately the free-cash-flow series of [-$35.1M, -$20.9M, $110.9M] newest first crosses zero, so neither cycle flag can compute a ratio - the OSIS condition - and the $110.9 million year belongs to a portfolio that has since been divested. Averaging a pre-divestiture peak against two post-divestiture negative years produces a $21.7 million base that describes no company that exists.
key_risks: Total liquidity of $25.0 million ($10.0 million cash plus about $15.0 million availability) against a development programme the company wants to accelerate
Single offshore federal-waters asset at Beta with a pipeline-incident history; Bairoil depends on a CO2 purchase agreement
Royalty relief is subject to commodity-price thresholds - approximately $92 per BOE trailing twelve-month average - and can be suspended
An unremediated material weakness is still listed among the company's own risks
Q3 operating cash flow of $3.1 million against a $10.8 million adjusted EBITDA shows weak conversion
watch_for: Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 operating cash flow with a full quarter of Special Case Royalty Relief and the Bairoil savings - the first clean read on the improved economics
The 2026 10-K reserve disclosure: PV-10 and the PDP decline rate, which are the honest anchors for an E&P and were not in the quarterly filings
Whether the buyback continues or liquidity forces it to stop
